header.title: Groups by MYCN expression, top 15 %: MYCN-high 53 vs rest 294. Expression-defined, not a clinical call.
header.research_use: Research use only; not for clinical use.

summary.plain: 64 plates, 366 samples and 24,576 reactions. 58 genes compared between MYCN-high (53 units) and rest (294). At the planned analysis 11 genes are up, 29 down and 18 have no call; 21 keep their call in fewer than 80 % of the 744 analyses qPilot checks. The audit finds 23 genes solid and 5 fragile.

methods.plain:
Raw fluorescence of 24,576 reactions on 64 plates (366 samples) was read from the RDML file data_vermeulen_raw.rdml (RDML version 1.4; SHA-256 bc1d233e3866ad4d32736a9feea832ea6261a9c75d82a78e465d31bad554e151). These are the published neuroblastoma data of Vermeulen et al., as redistributed for the curve-analysis benchmark of Ruijter and colleagues.

Each well's baseline, amplification efficiency and starting quantity (N0) were estimated with LinRegPCR, using the RDML consortium's rdmlpython vendored unchanged at commit fce7a44e8b47b90759c646b557de568f7af77e75; Cq is TD0, the cycle where the third derivative of the curve crosses zero (qPilot compares N0, not Cq). Each assay's efficiency is the mean of its wells' individual efficiencies, from 1.73 to 1.94 across the 64 assays (median 1.90), as amplification factor per cycle; N0 uses that mean. A curve counts as amplified by LinRegPCR's own call (a starting quantity was found). Of 23,423 sample wells, 323 (1.4 %) gave no quantity; they were left out (Drop empty wells). A person excluded 1 well: ODC1_20080226/A3.

The 5 candidate control genes (ALUsq(Eurogentec), HMBS, HPRT1, SDHA(1) and UBC(2)) were ranked by geNorm stability M: M from 1.63 (HPRT1) to 2.03 (UBC(2)); none is below the usual cut-off M 1.5, and the lowest pairwise variation V is 0.33 (usual cut-off 0.15). Each gene's quantity was divided by the geometric mean of 5 control genes (ALUsq(Eurogentec), HMBS, HPRT1, SDHA(1) and UBC(2)) in each biological unit, on the log2 scale; this is the recommended option and the choice is still open. Between the groups, 3 of 10 control-gene pairs shift by at least 1.4× (largest HMBS:UBC(2): 1.8×, p 0.058).

Biological units were split by the expression of MYCN(4): the top 15 % form the MYCN-high group (53 units) and the rest the reference group (294 units); the groups are defined from the data, not by a clinical call. Technical replicates were averaged within each biological unit (mean log2 N0) and never counted as n. Each gene was compared between the groups with Welch's t-test on per-unit log2 normalised quantities; fold changes are reported with 95 % confidence intervals. A gene is called up or down only if p < 0.05 and the change is at least 2-fold; otherwise it has no call. No correction for multiple testing was applied across the 58 genes. At this analysis 11 genes are up, 29 down and 18 have no call.

Every conclusion was recomputed under the 744 analyses qPilot checks (qPilot's choice grid: every combination of 31 control-gene sets, 3 group cut-offs, 2 rules for wells without a quantity and 4 amplification-call rules). 21 of 58 genes keep their call in fewer than 80 % of them. The control genes alone change 31 calls, the group cut-off alone 17, the amplification-call rule alone 11 and the rule for wells without a quantity alone 0.

The analysis choices are recorded in a hash-chained decision log (1 entry; head 63011ae06c81fe00c5805c17a1f9188c0edf0521f7517c8093a4fb282610fc62). Which control genes to normalise to: Recommended set (all five), the recommended option; still open (another option changes at least one conclusion). Where to cut the comparison groups: Top 15 % by MYCN expression, the recommended option; still open (another option changes at least one conclusion). Which curves count as amplified: LinRegPCR's own call (a starting quantity was found), the recommended option; still open (another option changes at least one conclusion). What to do with wells that never amplified: Drop empty wells, set automatically because no option changes a conclusion here. In Studio, 247 proposals about the design and the curves were made (137 by rules and 110 by a model); a person accepted 128 and rejected 119 before the design and the curves were confirmed.

A robustness audit (qPilot's Decision Simulator, qsim 0.1.0) re-ran the confirmed study under every combination of 8 analysis decisions (90,396 analyses), after reproducing qPilot's comparison of all 58 genes (largest difference in log2 fold change 5e-15). In the audit's reasonable set (144 analyses: no shortcuts such as single or paired control genes; groups and multiplicity as planned), 23 genes are solid, 7 hold with caveats, 3 depend on the choices, 5 are fragile, 2 need their data checked first and 18 have no call. It was run at the decision log's current head.

Analysis with qPilot 0.1.0 on Python 3.12.14; LinRegPCR from rdmlpython (MIT licence), geNorm reimplemented from its paper and Welch's test from SciPy's t distribution, and the audit with qPilot's Decision Simulator. The study's Analysis Record (the input file, every decision and their checksums) re-runs to the same numbers with qpilot rerun. Reported following MIQE 2.0; the checklist is attached.
